subject: Food Science
title: Mold on Food
description: Learn Mold on Food in one minute.

hook.text: That fuzzy spot on bread is just the visible part. Mold roots penetrate deep—far beyond what you can see.

buildup.text: Molds are fungi that grow as branching filaments called hyphae. They spread through microscopic spores in the air.

discovery.text: Some molds produce mycotoxins—toxic compounds that cause liver damage, cancer, and immune suppression.

twist.text: Cutting mold off soft cheese or bread doesn't help—hyphae extend invisibly throughout the food. Hard cheese is safer to trim.

climax.text: Aspergillus flavus produces aflatoxin—one of the most potent natural carcinogens. It contaminates peanuts and corn.

punchline.text: Mold you see is the tip of the iceberg. The real problem is invisible.

quiz.question: Why can't you just cut mold off soft cheese?
options: Invisible mold filaments extend deep throughout the food
